experimental evidence does not suggest one theory over the other, then both are equally valid. A given
physicist might prefer one theory over another on the grounds that one seems more simple, more natural, or
more beautiful than the other, but that physicist would quickly acknowledge that he or she cannot say the
other theory is invalid. Rather, he or she would be honest about the fact that more experimental evidence is
needed to determine which theory is a better description of nature.
